subject: Cloud Computing
title: The Three-Tier Architecture
description: Learn The Three-Tier Architecture in one minute.

hook.text: Presentation, logic, data — three layers that have powered web applications for over 25 years.

buildup.text: The frontend shows the UI. The backend processes logic. The database stores data. Each tier scales independently.

discovery.text: Cloud makes three-tier easy: a CDN for the frontend, containers for the backend, managed database for data.

twist.text: Modern apps are outgrowing three tiers. Caching layers, message queues, and APIs add more complexity between them.

climax.text: Three-tier is a starting point, not a ceiling. Most production systems evolve into something richer over time.

punchline.text: Three tiers got us this far. Real systems need more layers.

quiz.question: What are the three tiers in traditional three-tier architecture?

details.summary: Three-tier architecture separates an application into presentation, logic, and data layers. Each tier can scale, update, and fail independently. It remains the default starting point for most web applications deployed in the cloud.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding three-tier architecture provides the foundation for every more advanced cloud pattern. Most production systems still follow this model or evolve from it.
takeaways: Presentation, logic, and data tiers are deployed separately
Each tier can scale independently based on demand
It remains the baseline for most cloud-hosted web apps

faq.question: What are the three tiers in three-tier architecture?
faq.answer: The presentation tier handles the user interface, the logic tier processes business rules and application logic, and the data tier stores and retrieves persistent data. Each tier communicates through well-defined interfaces.

faq.question: When should you move beyond three-tier architecture?
faq.answer: When individual components need different scaling profiles, deployment cadences, or technology stacks, a microservices or event-driven approach may be more appropriate. Three-tier works well for moderate complexity and smaller teams.
